messages:
Olivia (sales): Heads-up — Velora just confirmed a last-minute live demo in ~2h for eu customers. They need low-latency generation for ~15m burst. Current per-project concurrency will queue them hard. Can we get a temporary quota/burst unblock for project `velora` in eu-west2? Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4521 :pray:

Raj (eng-runtime): What's their expected QPS / concurrency? Which model and token sizes? Also need current shard utilisation + queue length for eu-west2 to assess safety.

Olivia (sales): Rough numbers from product: model `redwood-4o-quant` (chat), avg seq ~120 tokens, expected sustained qps ~120, peak burst ~400 qps for ~10-15 minutes. Primary concern is demo latency, they can't tolerate long queueing.

Mia (support): Pasting recent metrics (30m window):
```
queue_length: 352
avg_serving_latency: 420ms
p95_latency: 1.2s
gpus_total: 48
gpus_in_use: 47 (98%)
active_projects_on_shard: 12
current_project_concurrency(velora): 52
```
Link to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/eu-west2/serving

OpsBot: ALERT — eu-west2 shard saturation detected. Admission control rate limiting active for low-priority routes. Event id: ob-2026-1785554321

Raj (eng-runtime): Ack. With GPUs at ~98% there is risk of tail SLO violations if we blindly raise global capacity. Options: 1) Temporarily bump velora's per-project concurrency + burst allowance with a short TTL + strict per-customer rate cap; 2) Put velora on a higher-priority lane with preemptive eviction of low priority work; 3) Route demo traffic to `redwood-3o` fallback for degraded perf but lower GPU footprint; 4) Spin ephemeral dedicated slice (but takes 10-30m to warm).

Raj (eng-runtime): My recommended quick path: create a temporary quota override for velora: concurrency -> 300, burst allowance -> 400 qps, TTL 3h, attach automatic fallback to `redwood-3o-quant` if queue > 200, and set billing/cost hold so Sales accepts overage. Add an emergency alert to rollback if p95>2s or GPU util >99.5%.

SRE Oncall: Concern — bumping to 300 concurrent could starve other tenants and risk OOMs on KV cache. We need to enforce per-connection token cap and ensure KV cache prewarm. Also require that Sales ack costs and customer cover spike overage.

Olivia (sales): Sales confirms customer will accept a billed demo overage (Velora agreed). Please proceed if SRE approves.

Mia (support): I can implement the override via admin CLI now. Proposed command: 
```
admin-cli quota override \
  --project velora \
  --region eu-west2 \
  --concurrency 300 \
  --burst 400 \
  --ttl 3h \
  --rate-limit 400qps \
  --fallback redwood-3o-quant \
  --safeguards "p95_latency<2s,gpu_util<99.5" \
  --note "Velora paid demo; ticket OPS-4521"
```
Who should I tag for the approval step?

Raj (eng-runtime): Tag SRE Oncall and me. Also add `--max_tokens_per_request 512` to prevent insane token sweeps.

Mia (support): Updated command and issuing now.

OpsBot: QUOTA_OVERRIDE_APPLIED — id: qo-2026-1785554321-7f9a. Effective immediately. TTL 3h.

SRE Oncall: Monitoring. If p95 > 2s or queue_length > 250 for more than 2 consecutive minutes, auto-rollback policy will trigger. Also enabling a temporary canary: first 10% of velora traffic hits `redwood-4o-quant`, rest goes to `redwood-3o-quant` if util stays high.

Raj (eng-runtime): Running a quick smoke check: `kubectl logs -n serving shard-eu-west2 -f | grep velora` — looks like KV cache misses high but warming. Keep an eye on memory.

Mia (support): Smoke check OK. Current queue length dropped from 352 -> 48 after override, avg latency now ~380ms.

Olivia (sales): Amazing — Velora is live and demo running. They reported acceptable latencies so far. :tada:

SRE Oncall: Reminder to revert override after demo window ends. I'll schedule a rollback at TTL expiry + 15m cushion unless we receive a manual extend request.

Olivia (sales): Please send me the final cost delta after.

Raj (eng-runtime): Postmortem action: add a faster path for demo bursts (pre-warm API that reserves small dedicated slice) and a templated override flow for sales with soft cost approvals. Filed as follow-up: INFRA-1992.

Mia (support): Closing OPS-4521 with note: temporary override applied and auto-rollback configured.

Olivia (sales): Great teamwork, thanks everyone. :heart:
